the T-026 wing in ground effect is a complex and challenging flow, and while the data are a good source of validation for two-dimensional numerical investigations, it is not clear that a single set of mesh and turbulence modeling parameters can be used to accurately model the flow for a range of angles of incidence, ground clearances, and aspect ratios.

the numerical schemes investigated in this paper are capable of predicting the flow over a double element wing in ground effect, but the choice of turbulence model and numerical scheme is critical to the accuracy of the results, and that the results of the simulations presented in this paper are sensitive to the choice of turbulence models, numerical schemes, and meshes.
there is no single best approach for numerical simulations of ground-effect flows, and the best approach for a given problem will depend on the application and the desired accuracy of the solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 2D RANS simulations of the ground effect flows over the Tyrell 026 airfoil are able to predict the overall trend of the lift and pressure distributions, but the quantitative results are not in good agreement with experimental data.

the numerical simulations are in good qualitative agreement with the experimental data and the numerical results are in good quantitative agreement with the experimental results for the 80% T-026 profile at a range of angles of attacks, ground clearances, and Reynolds numbers.
we found the most accurate numerical results were obtained using a mesh resolution of at least 1 million cells, and the Spalart-Allmaras turbulence model with a wall function approach.
